newsitem.title: UK: Fergie drops bid to block revealing memoirs.
newsitem.headline: Fergie drops bid to block revealing memoirs.

text.p: Britain's Duchess of York on Thursday pulled out of an attempt to prevent publication of a book that threatened to reveal intimate details of her affair with her former "financial adviser," John Bryan.

Her decision came just days before the case was due to be heard at London's High Court where the Duchess, better known as Fergie, could have been called to give evidence in public about her private life.
"The matter has been resolved. An agreement has been reached with her lawyers," a publishing industry source told Reuters.

The ex-wife of Queen Elizabeth's second son, Prince Andrew, was seeking to block publication of "Fergie, Her Secret Life" by Allan Starkie, a former friend of Bryan's. The book will now be published on November 4.

Her publishers said that Fergie, who was called on by the court to provide 500,000 pounds ($780,000) as security against losing the case, had decided not to go ahead after receiving assurances that the book would not contain any material damaging to the royal family.
While still married to Andrew, Fergie was photographed frolicking with Bryan, an American, in the south of France as her two young daughters looked on.
An infamous picture of Bryan sucking the toe of the topless duchess was splashed across newspapers and magazines worldwide.

It was a major embarrassment for the royal family as well as for Fergie herself, who has has come under attack from the press almost since the day of her engagement for her appearance, her free spending ways and latterly, her allegedly voracious sexual appetite.
Starkie said he did not believe he had betrayed Fergie or her former lover by writing the book.
"Truth has its own value. Truth is like water it finds its own level. I am not betraying anything that doesn't need to be said," he told a news conference called by his publisher.
"I decided to publish the information because I thought the story needed to be told. I thought the public had a need to understand what happened," said Starkie.

Starkie has been beaten into print by a faith healer who treated Fergie for stress for three years. The revelations by Madame Vasso that the duchess had at least two affairs while married to Andrew have been serialised in lurid detail in several tabloid newspapers this week.
The tabloids which revel in exposing intimate details of Fergie's love life and financial troubles are likely to be gravely disappointed at not seeing Fergie in the witness box.

They faced a similar letdown early last year when Fergie's former sister-in-law, Princess Diana, also dropped a court case over sneaked photographs taken of her exercising at her gym, just a few days before it was due to begin.
Diana was also expected to have been called to testify in court about her relationship with the media.

Fergie is due to publish her own memoirs next month and Starkie's publishers have accused her trying to block publication of "Fergie: Her Secret Life" to prevent it from damaging sales of her own book.
It said in September it would seek damages of two million pounds if her court case succeeded.
Fergie's memoirs will be limited by a clause in her divorce agreement which prevents her from revealing information about her life in the royal family.
As the announcement that Fergie was dropping the case was made, she was boarding a flight for New York for a charity engagement.
She and Starkie's publisher will each pay their own costs in the case, launched six weeks ago.
